I have been working this land for forty years. I know what it asks of me and what I can give it. My husband and I are getting older — two people, 16 mu, it is manageable if I do not overextend. We have the well, so water is not my worry. My worry is my back and whether the cotton price will be decent this year.

For the wheat-maize ground — I think about ten mu — I will do what I have always done. Wheat goes in after the autumn harvest. I will use the improved seed from the county supply station, the same variety I used last year that did well. I put down base fertilizer before plowing — compound fertilizer plus urea topdress at jointing. Four waterings for wheat: before winter, at jointing, heading, and grain fill. For maize, I sow right after wheat harvest in June. I buy hybrid seed — everyone does now, it yields much more. Maize needs water at tasseling and grain fill, maybe three times total. I use rotary tillage before wheat, and for maize I just direct seed into the stubble — the machine service does it now.

The remaining six mu or so I keep in cotton. Cotton is harder work, many pesticide sprays for bollworm and aphids, but I have done it my whole life. I know when to spray by looking at the leaves. I plow the cotton ground properly in spring before transplanting. Cotton needs more waterings through the hot summer — maybe five times from the well.

I do not change things that work. This is what my hands know.
